primitives.note: Each slot is a toggled 'mood' that grants access to 3 distinct sub-spells (QQ/QW/QE, WQ/WW/WE, EQ/EW/EE); casting any sub-spell ends the mood and puts the whole slot on cooldown. The simulator needs to pick which sub-spell to cast each time the slot is off cooldown.
Passive mark: a damaging ability applies a 4s mark to a hit enemy; a different damaging ability landing on the marked target consumes the mark and creates a separate bonus-damage explosion.

QQ (Devastating Fire) adds bonus damage scaled to the target's max health (capped vs monsters); QW (Severing Bolt) adds a large damage multiplier if it hits only one enemy or an immobilized enemy, scaled by the target's missing health - both conditions are effectively always true against a lone dummy.
QE (Molten Fissure) leaves ticking lava fissures (0.25s ticks over 2.5s) after each explosion; R (Spiraling Despair) applies a ticking aura (damage every 0.25s over 3s) before its final explosion.

QE fires 7 separate timed explosion shockwaves from one cast (each a separate damage instance, plus the DoT fissures they leave); R has a separately-timed initial hit, a DoT aura, and a final explosion instance, each a distinct damage source.

Stirring Lights (WE) arms Hwei's next 3 basic attacks or ability hits (within 9s) to each deal bonus magic damage; relevant to the damage fight as extra magic damage riders on subsequent casts/attacks.

Every sub-spell has its own mana cost (50-120) charged only on the actual cast (not on toggling the mood); with 4 spell slots all costing mana this can meaningfully cap casts across 15s, especially combined with Stirring Lights' mana restore.

needsBespoke.why: Hwei's kit is three independent 3-way stance-selection systems (Q/W/E moods) layered on top of a cross-ability mark-and-detonate passive that explicitly requires the triggering hit to come from a *different* damaging ability/cast instance than the one that applied the mark. No single closed-list primitive captures 'pick 1 of 3 sub-spells per slot, then chain casts across slots so each new hit detonates the previous ability's mark for bonus damage.' Correctly simulating maximum damage requires custom logic that (1) chooses the best sub-spell per mood each time a slot is off cooldown, and (2) sequences casts across Q/W/E/R so consecutive damaging hits alternate abilities to keep re-triggering Signature of the Visionary, rather than a fixed proc-on-primitive.

proposal: Pre-fight: toggle Serenity (W) into Stirring Lights (WE) and cast it immediately so its 3 empowered hits are ready to buff the opening abilities/attacks.
Open with Spiraling Despair (R) down the lane at the dummy to start its damage-over-time aura and apply the passive mark on the initial hit.

Immediately follow with a Q-mood cast (toggle Disaster then cast Severing Bolt, QW) targeted on the dummy: this is a different ability than R, so it detonates R's mark for the passive's bonus explosion, and QW's isolation/missing-health bonus is large against a lone target.
As soon as Q is off cooldown again, alternate into the E-mood (toggle Torment then cast Grim Visage, EQ, the fastest-cast E option) to re-apply a fresh mark and add more raw magic damage.

Continue weaving Q (whichever of QQ/QW/QE currently does the most damage against the dummy's remaining health/resists) and E (EQ/EW/EE) sub-spells back-to-back on cooldown for the rest of the 15s, always alternating which ability casts last so each new hit can detonate the previous ability's passive mark.

Use basic attacks in dead time between casts to consume Stirring Lights charges and keep DPS continuous; do not waste time on W's non-damaging sub-spells (WQ/WW) since they contribute no damage in a dummy fight.
Do not use Wash Brush during the fight - it only exits a mood for free but forfeits that mood's cast, i.e. it produces no damage and only wastes time in a max-DPS sequence.
R is only cast once at the opener given its long cooldown (120/100/80s) relative to the 15s fight window.
questions: Given the dummy's assumed health/resist values, which specific QQ/QW/QE and EQ/EW/EE sub-spells actually maximize total damage in 15s - is QW's isolation/missing-health multiplier reliably the best Q option, or does QQ's max-health-ratio bonus win against tankier dummy stats?
